proxy_language: Classical Nahuatl (Central Mexican Nahuatl, 16th-century attested form) as a weak areal proxy; 'Talumnuod' is not a known historical culture
proxy_rationale: No attested people or language called Talumnuod exists in the literature. The label 'Atlantic Americas' with a late court-type polity is vague. The only well-documented court-language tradition in the Americas with rich documentation of courtly naming is Classical Nahuatl (Aztec Triple Alliance), though its Gulf of Mexico side touches the Atlantic basin. Alternatives (Taino/Arawakan, Tupi-Guarani, Mayan) are less suited to court vocabulary. The link is purely areal and typological, not genealogical; the current game strings (Vozin de jike, Fosigab) fit no known Americas language and should be rebuilt.
phonology: Classical Nahuatl consonants: p t k kw (written cu/qu) ? (saltillo, written h or omitted), ts (tz), tl (a lateral affricate), ch, s, x [sh], l, m, n, w (hu/uh), y. Vowels a e i o, with contrastive length (often unmarked in transliteration). No b d g f r v z in native words. Stress is penultimate. The saltillo is a glottal stop, often weak or unwritten.
phonotactics: Syllable shapes (C)V(V)(C). No word-initial clusters; medial clusters of two consonants are common (nc, mp, ht, tl). tl is a single phoneme, and word-final -tl is the absolutive suffix. Final consonants are limited to -l, -n, -tl, -tli, -h, -c (q/c), and -tzin is reverential. No voiced stops, no f, r, b, d, g, v. Vowel sequences are mostly across morpheme boundaries.
orthography: Standard Classical Nahuatl (Carochi/Andrews/Launey) orthography: qu before e/i, c before a/o, cu for /kw/, hu for /w/ (uh word-finally), tz for /ts/, tl, ch, x, z for /s/ before a/o and c before e/i (Andrews: z/c), h for saltillo, optional macrons for long vowels. Written in lowercase for audit purposes.
morphology: Polysynthetic-leaning agglutinating, suffixing and prefixing. Nouns have an absolutive suffix: -tl / -tli / -li (atl 'water', cihuatl 'woman', calli 'house') that drops when possessed or in compounds. Possessive prefixes: no- 'my', mo- 'your', i- 'his/her', to- 'our'. Plural: -tin (animates) or -me, or reduplication, with -meh as the Andrews form. Reverential -tzin. Locative suffixes -c, -co, -tlan, -tla, -pan, -nahuac, -tech. Diminutive -ton/-pil. Place names are formed with noun + locative suffix.
compounding: Noun-noun compounds are head-final: the modifier precedes the head, the modifier loses its absolutive suffix, e.g. cihua-pilli 'noblewoman'. Possession is shown by a possessive prefix on the head: i-calli in tlatoani 'the ruler's house'. 'Place of X' = X + -tlan/-tla/-co: Tenochtitlan, Mexico. 'Maker of X' agentive = X + verb-stem + -qui/-ni or tla- + verb + -ni: tlacuiloani 'painter'. Titles are often head-final: tlahtoani 'speaker'. Names of courtly offices: tlacochcalcatl 'keeper of the dart house'.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier before head (adjective/noun + noun). Possessor precedes possessed with the possessive prefix on the possessed noun. Relative clauses and demonstratives are mostly preposed (in = the). Locative/postpositional phrases follow the noun as suffixes.

worked_examples.name: Acalli
worked_examples.gloss: a(tl) 'water' + calli 'house' (absolutive dropped; Acalli is the standard word for boat)

notes: Talumnuod is not an attested culture; the proxy is a speculative areal choice and is explicitly not claimed as the culture's real language. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since Nahuatl is not Goidelic. Native Nahuatl lacks b d g f r v and word-initial clusters, so names like 'Vozin de jike' and 'Fosigab' do not conform. The forbidden_patterns list is a heuristic audit aid for lowercase Latin-script names, not a full phonotactic parser.
